newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-Australia November retail trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-Australia November retail trade.

text.p: Australian retail trade rose 0.7 percent in November after a 1.4 percent increase in October, according to data released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Forecasts had centred on a 1.0 percent rise.
The ABS also said building approvals for November fell 1.6 against an expected 2.0 percent fall and after a 12.8 percent increase the previous month.
The following are a selection of immediate economists' reactions to the data.
CRAIG JAMES, SENIOR ECONOMIST, COLONIAL STATE BANK

"There was very modest growth in retail sales, towards the lower end of expectations. On a trend basis, we're now seeing three consecutive falls, which shows that things are still fairly flat in retail land.

"(The building approvals data) continues the modest recovery that we've been seeing. There's nothing spectacular in terms of new dwelling activity. A modest uptrend is continuing on a trend basis and we expect that to continue through 1997."
